one_line: Early Indo-Greek king of the northwest who pioneered bilingual coinage for a diverse Indo-Greek-Indian economy.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, athletic but not bulky, with the lean build of a cavalry commander accustomed to travel and field inspections.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, high cheekbones, and a short well-groomed beard and moustache; light olive complexion sun-browned from the Punjab heat; sharp, thoughtful eyes under slightly furrowed brows, default expression a calm, analytical half-smile as if weighing policy and profit.
appearance.hair: Short, wavy dark brown hair cut above the neck, with a subtle laurel-like metal circlet (simple Greek diadem band in dull silver) resting low across the forehead, hair brushed back from the temples but not long enough to tie.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate Indo-Greek royal field attire: a long-sleeved Greek-style tunic (chiton) of undyed off-white linen reaching mid-thigh and belted at the waist with a narrow dark brown leather belt; over it a knee-length sleeved riding coat in muted teal-blue wool (inspired by Hellenistic cavalry coats adapted to local climate) with a wrap-over front secured by a simple round bronze brooch at the right shoulder; loose but narrow-ankled trousers in soft terracotta-red cotton/linen, borrowing from Central Asian and local fashions; sturdy calf-height leather boots in dark brown with simple lacing, suitable for moving between city, port and countryside; over his shoulders a lightweight pale sand-coloured cloak with a subtle narrow Greek meander border in darker teal along its edge, draped so one side can be pulled over his left arm; minimal jewellery: a single signet ring on his right hand and a discrete pair of small gold stud earrings echoing Hellenistic taste adapted to local norms.
appearance.signature: A large, square silver coin held between his fingers and a smaller round coin in his other hand, both clearly showing (without text) one side with an elephant and the other with a humped bull and nandipada symbol, representing his bilingual and bicultural coinage as his constant prop.

ref_desc: Apollodotus I is a light-olive, sharp-eyed Indo-Greek king in his early 30s with short wavy dark-brown hair, a simple silver diadem, off-white tunic, teal-blue riding coat, terracotta trousers, sand cloak, dark-brown boots, and Indo-Greek elephant-and-bull coins in hand.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Apollodotus I, an Indo-Greek king in his early 30s with an athletic build, light-olive complexion, oval face, sharp thoughtful eyes, short wavy dark-brown hair, and a simple silver diadem band low on his forehead; give him a short well-groomed beard and moustache and a calm, analytical half-smile; dress him in an off-white knee-length linen tunic belted with a narrow dark-brown leather belt, over which he wears a muted teal-blue wool riding coat with long sleeves and a wrap-over front pinned on the right shoulder by a round bronze brooch, paired with loose but tapered terracotta-red trousers and sturdy calf-height dark-brown leather boots; drape a pale sand-beige cloak with a narrow darker teal Greek meander border over his shoulders, one side free to wrap around his left arm, and add small gold stud earrings and a single signet ring; place in his hands his signature props: a large square silver coin between the fingers of one hand and a smaller round coin in the other, each side showing an elephant on one face and a humped bull with nandipada symbol on the other (no readable text), emphasizing him as a ruler focused on bilingual coinage and trade; use a restrained palette of off-white, teal-blue, terracotta-red, sand beige, and dark brown, and show front, three-quarter, and back views to capture consistent face, hair, costume, and coins without any background distractions.
